title: client-window-sampling-and-auth-replay-notes
content:
Scratchpad: client window sampling & auth replay experiments

Context
- Observed customer reports: brief bursts of 401s followed by 429s when client rotates API keys (esp mobile SDKs) or when many ephemeral tokens land in the system within a short span.
- Hypothesis set: (A) per-client fixed-window quota causing bursts to see 429 after ephemeral key churn; (B) auth middleware returning 401 for stale keys during rotation and replayed requests are then throttled; (C) clock drift / caching causing token verification failures that flip to 429 once requests are retried; (D) rate-limit key grouping by client_id + fingerprint mis-bucketing requests.

Repro plan notes (quick experiments run from my laptop)
- Environment: staging cluster in us-west2, routing -> serving-runtime canary (serving-runtime:v2025-10-26-canary).
- Test keys: sk-test-window-A (long-lived), sk-test-ephemeral-1..10 (ephemeral TTL 60s)

Commands tried (examples)
1) Simple generator request, single key
curl -s -X POST
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-window-A"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b", "input":"hello"}' | jq
Expected: 200
Observed: 200 consistently (baseline)

2) Burst with ephemeral keys (20 requests across 10 keys in ~10s)
for i in {1..20}; do KEY=sk-test-ephemeral-$(( (i%10)+1 )); curl -s -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"ping"}' & done; wait
Observed: mixture of 200, some 401 (about 10%), then several 429s clustered ~5-8s after initial 401s.
Sample 401 body:
{
  "error": {"message": "Unauthorized: key not recognized", "code": 401}
}
Sample 429 body:
{
  "error": {"message": "Rate limit exceeded", "code": 429, "retry_after": 3},
  "meta": {"grouping":"client_window:sk-client-123","window_start":"2025-10-28T14:03:00Z"}
}

3) Rapid replay with same ephemeral key after 401
- Immediately after a 401 with ephemeral key E1, re-sent the exact request with same key E1 within 400ms.
Observed: sometimes returns 401 again, sometimes flips to 429. When 429, meta.grouping shows shared client window (client_id fingerprint).

4) Clock drift check (JWT iat/exp validation)
- Created tokens with iat artificially ahead/behind by 30s and 120s.
- Verified auth-service logs: tokens with iat > now + 60s are rejected with 401 (clock skew guard).
- But most customer replays show iat within acceptable range.

5) Header manipulation / missing fields (edge cases)
- Requests missing 'User-Agent' or with truncated Authorization header result in 401 at auth layer.
- Some mobile SDKs split headers across TCP packets; rare but saw 401 in those cases.

Observations / patterns
- 401 often happens in first seen request after key rotation. 429s tend to appear shortly after as the system attributes replay volume to a single client fingerprint.
- Meta.grouping in 429 responses points to per-client window (server groups ephemeral keys under same client fingerprint).
- The transition 401 -> 429 indicates two subsystems interacting: auth decision (401) and rate-limiter attribution (429). If a request is rejected by auth and immediately retried, the retry may still be counted against the client window (we need to confirm whether rate-limiter increments on rejected auth attempts).
- Auth-service returns 401 with generic message; no explicit 'stale_key' code. That forces client-side guessing.

Logs I pulled (redacted)
- auth-svc: ERROR token-verify: token not found (token_id=ephemeral-7) at 2025-10-28T14:03:01.341Z
- rl-svc: incr-window client=sk-client-123 window_start=2025-10-28T14:03:00 count=1 source=ingress request_id=abc123
- auth-svc: token-issue: rotated old_key=sk-client-12 -> new_key=sk-client-13 at 2025-10-28T14:03:02.012Z
- rl-svc: incr-window client=sk-client-123 count=18 window_start=2025-10-28T14:03:00 (exceeded)

Hypotheses refined
- H1: When keys rotate, some in-flight requests still hit old auth cache and receive 401. Retries then hit the rate-limiter and are associated with the same client fingerprint, causing 429 bursts.
- H2: Rate-limiter is counting all requests (including those rejected by auth) towards the window. If true, rejected auth attempts amplify quota usage.
- H3: Client fingerprinting groups ephemeral keys by client_id header + X-Forwarded-For; misconfigurations cause many distinct tokens to collapse into a single bucket.

Quick checks to validate H2
- Instrumented rl-svc to emit counter when request hits rate limiter pre-auth vs post-auth (local build).
- Result: rl-svc increments happen at ingress before auth decision ~85% of the time. That explains 401 + subsequent 429.
- Action: move increment to post-auth or add separate counters for rejected requests.

Mitigations tested (staging)
- Short-term tweak: when auth-svc rejects due to 'token not found', return 401 with header 'Retry-After: 5' and 'X-RateLimit-Bypass: true' signifying rl-svc should not count the request. Implemented a patch on staging where rl-svc checks auth verdict header; initial tests reduced 429 secondary spikes by ~60%.
- Longer-term: adjust rate-limiter to perform attribution after auth or maintain separate rejection budget. Also consider returning distinct error codes for stale/rotated keys to enable clients to do smarter backoffs.

Failed experiments / dead ends
- Tried disabling rate-limiter for requests with 'X-Debug-Bypass: 1' — reduces data fidelity and not acceptable for prod.
- Tried increasing ephemeral token TTL to reduce rotation frequency; improved but not acceptable for security policy.

Open questions / next steps
- Confirm whether any front proxy (nginx/ADAPTER) is aggregating headers in a way that collapses client fingerprints. Need SRE to review ingress header normalization. (Assigned to Jordan.)
- Decision: move rl increment to post-auth vs implement an auth-reject filter in rl-svc. Pros/cons documented in internal PR. (See linked PR.)
- Product: communicate to SDK teams to add jittered exponential backoff on 401s during rotation windows rather than tight immediate retry. Add specific guidance to mobile SDK doc. (Priya owning outreach.)
- Add telemetry: tag rate-limit increments with auth-result (success/failed) for 30d retention to analyze impact.

Immediate action items
- [ ] Prod patch: respect auth-reject header in rl-svc for 2 weeks ramp (Maya + Jordan)
- [ ] SDK guidance update + sample backoff code (Priya)
- [ ] Add alert if %401->429 transition rate > 1% for any client in one minute (SRE)

Notes to self
- Keep reproducer script (ephemeral burst) handy; add more granular timings and per-request tracing id.
- When filing customer RCA, call out interplay between auth and rl subsystems as root cause (not just "rate limit spike").

Appendix: quick reproducer (bash)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
KEYS=(sk-test-ephemeral-1 sk-test-ephemeral-2 sk-test-ephemeral-3 sk-test-ephemeral-4 sk-test-ephemeral-5)
for i in {1..50}; do
  K=${KEYS[$((i % ${#KEYS[@]}))]}
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} $K\n" -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"check"}' &
  if (( i % 10 == 0 )); then sleep 0.5; fi
  done; wait

End of notes.
